Fujian Yongfu Power Engineering Co Ltd Resumes Operations After Insolvency Resolution

BEIJING, June 22 – Fujian Yongfu Power Engineering Co Ltd, a major player in China’s engineering and construction sector, has resumed operations after successfully concluding an insolvency process that had halted its business for several months, company officials said this week.

The company, based in Fuzhou, entered court-administered insolvency proceedings earlier this year following a prolonged cash-flow crisis and mounting debts. The move impacted ongoing infrastructure projects and left hundreds of employees in limbo as the firm’s future was determined by administrators.

In a statement released on Friday, Fujian Yongfu Power Engineering Co Ltd confirmed that the court approved its restructuring plan last week, effectively ending the insolvency process. “With the support of key stakeholders and a comprehensive reorganization of our financial commitments, we are now able to resume normal operations,” said Chen Jianhua, a member of the company’s senior management. “Our priority is to return to full capacity and ensure that our workforce is secure.”

Operations at several key construction sites in Fujian and neighboring provinces have already restarted, the statement said, with workers and subcontractors returning to their posts. According to the company, approximately 80% of its workforce is now back on site, and efforts are underway to bring the remaining personnel back within the next month.

Industry analysts noted that the resolution of Fujian Yongfu Power Engineering’s insolvency is a positive signal for the region’s construction sector, which has faced a series of high-profile collapses and liquidity challenges in recent years. “This outcome demonstrates that, even amid challenging conditions, restructuring can provide a viable path forward for struggling firms,” said Li Wei, an analyst at the China Construction Industry Association. “It will restore some confidence among suppliers and clients.”

The Fujian Construction Workers’ Union welcomed the news, calling it “a relief” for families who had faced uncertainty about wage payments and job security. “We appreciate the company’s efforts to ensure back pay is addressed and to involve workers in the transition process,” said union spokesperson Wu Lin.

While the company did not disclose the full terms of its restructuring, Chen said that agreements with creditors had been reached, allowing for the resumption of delayed projects. Local officials have also pledged support to ensure the company’s recovery and to minimize further disruptions to infrastructure development in the region.

Fujian Yongfu Power Engineering Co Ltd said it would publish an updated business plan next month and expects to meet its project delivery commitments for the remainder of the year.
